Priya — thanks for the redlines and clear asks. A few quick things from our side:

1) Primary data deletion: we can agree to a 30-day window for deletion from active stores once a verified erasure request is received (subject to legal hold).

2) Backups: we cannot commit to a 24-month default for all backups across every product tier. Operationally we can offer:
   - 90 days default backup retention for production snapshots, with an option to extend to 180 days for customers who need longer continuity and are on a dedicated plan.
   - For regulated customers with firm residency needs, we can provide onshore-only backup storage in US regions and an audit trail for access.

3) Certified proof-of-erasure: we can provide a playbook and a certified attestation process (internal verification + exportable audit logs). For backups specifically, erase-from-backup is operationally more complex; our standard approach is a tombstone/expire + overwrite window. We can provide an attestation of the wipe and verification steps within a bounded timeframe.

I'm attaching a short counterproposal that calls out a 180-day backup retention offer for Acme as an enterprise option, plus proposed language for onshore-only backup storage and attestation steps. If that looks workable, can we set a quick call?

Team — drafting guidance and proposed redline language below. I'm copying the final suggested wording into the DPA comments for legal review, but flagging pragmatic constraints up front.

Summary of proposed compromise (for Acme Health):
- Primary data deletion: Redwood will remove customer data from active stores within 30 days of a verified erase request, unless subject to a lawful hold.
- Backups: Redwood will offer an enterprise backup retention tier at 180 days. For standard customers the default backup retention is 90 days. Backups containing customer data will be confined to US regions for customers who purchase the enterprise backup offering. Backups will not be used for model training or analytics.
- Backup erasure process: Redwood's steps: 1) Mark snapshot for deletion (tombstone) immediately upon request; 2) Remove index references and prevent future restores; 3) Schedule physical overwrite as part of the next block-level scrub cycle (timeline: up to 180 days depending on storage medium).
- Certified attestation: Redwood will provide a signed certificate that includes: request id, customer id, deletion timestamp, system identifiers, and verification hashes/log excerpts. Standard issuance timeline: within 45 days of request; expedited (30-day) issuance available for legally compelled requests with a commercial escalation.
- Escrow option: If Acme requires contractual guarantee of physical overwrite beyond Redwood's standard processes, we will include an escrow carveout limited to litigation or regulatory holds. The escrow text will: (a) enumerate triggering conditions; (b) require Acme to provide written justification; (c) include auditability and cost recovery for escrow handling.

Redline extract (plain language):
"Upon receipt of a verified erasure request, Redwood shall delete Customer Data from active production storage within thirty (30) days, except to the extent subject to a lawful hold. For Customers who purchase the Enterprise Backup Retention option, Redwood will store backups within US-based regions and retain such backups for up to one hundred eighty (180) days. Redwood will provide a signed certificate of erasure containing request id, timestamp, affected systems, and verification logs within forty-five (45) days of completion of erasure. Expedited delivery (thirty (30) days) is available for legally compelled erasures upon request and subject to Redwood's escalation procedures. Backups will not be used for model training or analytics. Escrow arrangements for physical overwrite guarantees will be limited to litigation or regulatory holds and will be subject to additional fees and auditability requirements."

- Ben: confirm pricing and insert a billing line for the enterprise backup option in the proposal.
- Lauren: schedule a 30-minute redlines call with Acme Legal to walk through the compromise language and the attestation example.

I'll attach a sample certificate template and a sanitized log excerpt to the DPA comment thread.
